purpose: Machine-readable preliminary rulebook for detecting potential scalability and reliability risks in Python/FastAPI backend applications.

scope.principle: Static evidence identifies a potential risk pattern; runtime evidence is used to determine whether measurable impact occurs under a specified workload.
scope.research_status: All rules require literature verification before being treated as research-validated.

finding_policy.preferred_runtime_language: Observed impact under the tested workload.
finding_policy.causal_language: Use 'probable cause' unless causal evidence is sufficient.

severity_levels.low: Potentially minor impact or normally requires unusual conditions.
severity_levels.medium: Could materially affect performance/resource use under realistic workloads.
severity_levels.high: Could substantially increase resource consumption, latency, dependency load, or resource exhaustion risk under realistic scaling conditions.

rule_statuses.core: Recommended for the initial 7-week ScaleTrace prototype.
rule_statuses.extension: Useful extension if implementation time permits.
rule_statuses.experimental: Keep outside the core evaluation until framework/runtime semantics are validated.

rules.name: Database Query Inside Iterative Loop
rules.description: A database or ORM operation is executed inside a loop whose iteration count may grow with input or database cardinality.
rules.why: Database work may grow with the number of loop iterations, increasing query count, database load, and request latency.
static_evidence: database call nested inside for or while loop
ORM query/execute operation inside loop body
database dependency reachable from loop body
false_positives: data already cached by an abstraction
diagnostic_steps: measure query count under increasing input size
compare endpoint latency and database load
rules.test_case: Run the same endpoint with 10, 100, and 1000 records and determine whether query count grows with record count.

rules.name: Repeated Equivalent Database Operation
rules.description: Equivalent database operations are executed repeatedly within the same request or control-flow path without an evident need to repeat them.
rules.why: Redundant database work consumes database and application resources and may increase request latency.
static_evidence: repeated repository calls with equivalent arguments
same query signature on one control-flow path
false_positives: database state intentionally changes between calls
cache invalidation requires a fresh read
equivalent-looking calls have hidden side effects
diagnostic_steps: inspect whether results can safely be reused
rules.test_case: Instrument database access and verify whether one logical request executes the same logical lookup multiple times.

rules.name: ORM Relationship N+1
rules.description: Access to a lazily loaded ORM relationship occurs while iterating over parent entities, potentially causing one child query per parent.
rules.why: Query count can become proportional to the number of parent entities.
runtime_evidence: parent query followed by repeated child queries
rules.test_case: Create benchmark data with increasing numbers of parents and related records and compare generated query counts.

rules.name: Expensive Operation Inside Large Loop
rules.description: A potentially expensive CPU, allocation, parsing, sorting, serialization, or inference operation is repeatedly executed inside a loop.
rules.why: Repeated work can make execution cost grow with input size.
static_evidence: known expensive operation nested in loop
false_positives: operation is inexpensive for the tested inputs
rules.test_case: Benchmark increasing input sizes and determine whether CPU time grows disproportionately.

rules.name: Loop-Invariant Repeated Computation
rules.description: An expression or function call whose relevant inputs do not change within a loop is recomputed on every iteration.
rules.why: Loop-invariant work may be repeated unnecessarily.
static_evidence: arguments do not depend on loop variable
no visible mutation of relevant inputs
false_positives: mutation occurs through an indirect dependency
rules.test_case: Instrument the candidate function and verify whether invocation count equals loop iterations unnecessarily.

rules.name: Unbounded Full Dataset Materialization
rules.description: Potentially large or unbounded data is fully materialized in application memory.
rules.why: Memory consumption can grow with dataset size and may become a limiting resource.
static_evidence: absence of visible pagination or streaming
false_positives: dataset has a documented small upper bound
pagination is enforced by an outer layer
full materialization is required and bounded
rules.test_case: Run against progressively larger datasets and record process memory and latency.

rules.name: Unbounded Accumulation
rules.description: A collection grows repeatedly without a visible bound and may persist longer than the operation that created it.
rules.why: Persistent accumulation can increase memory consumption across requests or over long-running operations.
false_positives: collection is required for the final response
input itself has a strict documented limit
diagnostic_steps: observe whether memory returns to baseline
rules.test_case: Repeat the operation under a fixed workload and determine whether persistent memory usage increases over time.

rules.name: Blocking Operation in Async Request Handler
rules.description: A known blocking operation is executed directly inside an async FastAPI request handler.
rules.why: Blocking work can prevent the event loop from servicing other concurrent tasks.
false_positives: framework runs operation in a threadpool
operation is too small to create measurable contention
rules.test_case: Add a controlled blocking delay and compare concurrent throughput against an async-safe implementation.

rules.name: External Operation Without Explicit Timeout
rules.description: A supported external network operation has no visible timeout configuration.
rules.why: A slow dependency can keep request and connection resources occupied for an excessive period.
false_positives: timeout is injected through another abstraction
rules.test_case: Use a dependency that delays its response and verify that the application enforces a bounded wait.

rules.name: Unbounded or Aggressive Retry
rules.description: A failed operation is retried without a finite bound or without an appropriate delay/backoff.
rules.why: Retries can amplify downstream traffic and prolong resource occupancy.
false_positives: retry policy configured in a library
operation is deliberately retried under a bounded policy
rules.test_case: Force a dependency to fail repeatedly and verify that retry attempts remain bounded.

rules.name: Client or Pool Created Per Request
rules.description: A database or external-service client/pool is constructed inside a request handler rather than managed at an appropriate application lifecycle scope.
rules.why: Repeated construction can cause connection churn and unnecessary resource consumption.
false_positives: FastAPI dependency lifecycle manages resource reuse
rules.test_case: Compare connection creation under low and high concurrent request loads.

rules.name: Unbounded Concurrent Task Creation
rules.description: Asynchronous tasks are created proportional to an input collection without an explicit concurrency limit.
rules.why: Large task sets can increase memory use and overload downstream dependencies.
static_evidence: absence of visible semaphore or concurrency limiter
false_positives: input has a strict small upper bound
rules.test_case: Increase input size and observe task count, memory, and downstream calls.

rules.name: External Service Call Inside Loop
rules.description: An external network or service call occurs once per loop iteration.
rules.why: External call count and dependency latency can grow with input size.
static_evidence: network client call nested inside loop
loop variable used in request arguments
rules.test_case: Verify external call count for increasing input sizes.

rules.name: Sequential Independent External Calls
rules.description: Multiple external operations that appear independent are executed sequentially.
rules.why: Independent latency contributions can accumulate on the request critical path.
static_evidence: no obvious data dependency between call inputs
rules.test_case: Mock independent services with controlled latency and compare sequential and bounded-concurrent execution.

rules.name: Resource Acquired Without Visible Cleanup
rules.description: A resource is acquired without visible context management or cleanup.
rules.why: Repeated operations can accumulate open resources and eventually exhaust process or pool limits.
static_evidence: client construction without visible lifecycle management
rules.test_case: Repeat the operation and verify that resource count remains bounded.

rules.name: Cleanup Missing on Exceptional Path
rules.description: Cleanup appears on the normal path but may be skipped when an exception occurs.
rules.why: Exceptions can leave resources active and gradually exhaust bounded resource pools.
static_evidence: no visible finally or context manager
potential exception between acquisition and cleanup
rules.test_case: Force exceptions repeatedly and verify that resources are released after each failure.

implementation_contract.recommended_message_template: Potential {category} risk: {name}. Static evidence found at {file}:{line}. Runtime confirmation is {status}.
implementation_contract.rule_id_stability: Rule IDs must never be reused for a different rule. If a rule changes materially, create a new ID or increment the rulebook version.
